value: Quasi-steady burning observed in microgravity despite absence of air flow, notably in elevated-oxygen atmospheres considered for future spacecraft.
Chamber pressures were varied between tests but are not identified in the PSI summary table.

ACME insert in the Combustion Integrated Rack: ~100 L constant-volume chamber, mass-flow controllers, retracting resistively-heated igniter, 12-bit 1360x1024 colour camera with filter wheel, intensified OH*/CH2O cameras, radiometers, PMTs, thermocouple rake, SiC fibres, gas chromatograph.

value: CFI's PSI table identifies tests by a column named 'Flex Number' with values 1206-1387; FLEX's table numbers tests 1-274. The shared column name and MDCA/CIR hardware support one MDCA test-number series; numbers 275-1205 (presumably FLEX-2, which has no per-test PSI table) are undocumented in PSI.

SLICE: fan-driven flow duct with exchangeable burner tubes; SPICE: MSG flow duct with integrated nozzles and cameras; BASS: MSG, variable-speed fan up to 40 cm/s, Kanthal 29-gauge igniter; BASS-II: MSG forced flow with N2 vitiation. Same physical duct across all four: UNVERIFIED.
PSI record: E-FIELD 'is not being conducted to serve any space applications'. Challenge page claims E-FIELD mimicked partial gravity - not stated in PSI-22 record.
274 tests: end mode extinction 186, disruption 61, completion 27; fuels heptane 117, methanol 157; diluents N2, N2+CO2, N2+He; pressures ~0.7 atm (103), ~1 atm (161), 2-3 atm (9).
FLEX discovered quasi-steady cool-flame burning of n-heptane droplets after radiative extinction of the hot flame.
Saffire-I: large SIBAL sheet (94 x 40.6 cm) at 20 cm/s; concurrent burn 420 s vs opposed 70 s; flame stayed limited in size rather than growing continuously.
PSI contains no partial-gravity combustion runs (0 of 2,007 normalized combustion/aerosol rows).

Ambient-O2 basis (inverse-flame burner-stream O2 excluded). FIREWISE exploration envelope (O2 30-36% AND 8.2-10.2 psia): 0 runs. Challenge Moon-base definition (O2 >=30% AND P <=10.2 psia): 20 runs, all ACME CFI-G normal gas flames at 'approx p' 0.5066 bar (7.35 psia, reported), O2 32.3-38.9% (measured). Bracket within ~1 psia (O2 30-36%, 7.0-11.0 psia): 27 runs = 10 CFI-G (7.35 psia) + 17 FLEX droplets (10.33-10.50 psia, measured). Solids: 0 of 264 runs document pressure; 140 document O2 (max 22.2%), 124 document none.

value: Lunar-g Combustion Investigation flew on Blue Origin New Shepard NS-29 (2025-02-04); capsule spun at 11 RPM to simulate lunar gravity for >25 s; burned cotton-fiberglass fabric and a 4 mm PMMA rod; falling O2 used to define a limiting O2. Data not in PSI.

Flammability of Materials on the Moon: planned on CLPS CP-21, late 2026; 4 solid samples, quiescent, 21% O2 / 14.7 psia and 34% O2 / 8.2 psia; cameras, thermocouples, radiometers, O2 sensor. Launch status as of 2026-11-13 unverified.
Moon base atmosphere likely >=30% O2 at <=10.2 psi (challenge text); exploration atmosphere 34% O2 / 8.2 psia (FM2 poster); ISS 21% / 14.7 psia.

In ACME Flame Design and CFI-G inverse flames the XO2 column is the O2 mole fraction of the oxidizer stream issued from the burner into a fuel/N2 ambient; it is NOT the chamber atmosphere and must never be compared with a habitat atmosphere. 274 such rows (Flame Design 120, CFI-G 154).
source: PSI-10/PSI-159 'Inverse' experimental tables (columns XO2, Xf before/after test)
